s: Government of India Financial Inclusion Committee (2007-08) was chaired by
x: The Government of India's Committee on Financial Inclusion was chaired by Dr C. Rangarajan (constituted June 2006, final report January 2008).

s: Which committee is related to financial inclusion?
x: The C. Rangarajan Committee (2006-08) was the Committee on Financial Inclusion; Y.V. Reddy, Vaghul (money market) and Usha Thorat are not the financial inclusion committee.

s: Who among the following was the Chairman of the ‘Committee on Financial Inclusion’ constituted in January 2005?
x: The Committee on Financial Inclusion was chaired by Dr C. Rangarajan; it was actually constituted on 26 June 2006 (not January 2005) and reported on 4 January 2008. Subbarao, Ahluwalia and Kamal Nath did not chair it.

s: Which one of the following is not the objective of financial inclusion?
o: To extend financial services to poor population
To unlock the door of growth potential of weaker
To extend financial sector into rural areas
x: Financial inclusion seeks to expand banking infrastructure into underserved and rural areas, so shrinking it is not an objective; extending services to the poor, unlocking the growth potential of weaker sections and reaching rural areas are objectives.

s: Recently, a scheme named ‘Swabhimaan’ was launched. It’s main aim is :
o: To take banks to the doorsteps of the rural poor
To provide skill to rural artisans
To provide houses to BPL families
x: Swabhimaan (10 February 2011) was a financial inclusion campaign to take banking to the doorsteps of the rural poor; it was not a skills, women's empowerment or housing scheme.

s: Which of the following committees has given its recommendations on ‘financial inclusion’?
x: The C. Rangarajan Committee (2006-08) gave the recommendations on financial inclusion; Rakesh Mohan, Sinha and Kelkar committees dealt with other subjects.

s: Which one of the following is a hindrance in the process of financial inclusion?
x: Low income, illiteracy and a lack of bank branches all keep people out of the formal financial system, so 'all of the above' is the answer.

s: L.B.S. is one of the economic measures taken by the Government of India for financial inclusion. What is L.B.S. in this context?
x: LBS is the Lead Bank Scheme (written 'Lead Banking Scheme' in the stem), a district-level financial inclusion measure; the other expansions do not exist.

s: RBI has cleared the resolution to start Payment Banks in India for improving Financial Inclusion. Following committee had recommended the creation of Payment Banks :
x: The RBI's Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) on comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households recommended payments banks (differentiated banks); Mayaram, Reddy and Jalan did not.

s: ‘Financial Inclusion’ can be encouraged :
o: by issuing a ‘specific letter of credit’ to the deserving
by providing banking services to people of lower
by providing financial services to low income
x: Financial inclusion aims at basic banking and financial services for everybody, especially lower-income people, so all the listed means encourage it – 'all of the above'.

s: Financial inclusion as per RBI means
o: greater consumer protection for newly included customers.
an easily accessed and speedy grievance redressal process.
x: Financial inclusion as the RBI frames it goes with protection of newly included customers, quick grievance redressal and financial literacy, so 'All of the above' is the best answer.

s: ‘Swabhimaan Scheme’ launched in India is associated with :
x: Swabhimaan (10 February 2011) took banking to the doorsteps of the rural poor – it is about rural banking, not women's rights, old-age care or food security.

s: RBI had set up a committee to study and give suggestions on the microfinance sector. Its Chairman was :
x: The RBI Board sub-committee on the microfinance sector (October 2010), set up after the AP crisis, was chaired by Y.H. Malegam; Abid Hussain (small industry), Bimal Jalan and Rakesh Mohan headed other committees.

s: Who among the following was the Chairman of the Committee on Deepening Digital Payments appointed by the RBI?
x: The RBI's High-Level Committee on Deepening of Digital Payments (2019) was chaired by Nandan Nilekani; H.R. Khan, N.R. Narayana Murthy and Sanjay Jain did not chair it.

s:
Choose the correct statements about the "Pradhanamanthri Jan Dhan Yojana"

a) It was launched on 28th Aug 2014

b) It is aimed to provide bank accounts, insurance and debit card to all the citizens of India

c) Ministry of finance is the incharge of the scheme

d) It grants loans to the businessmen
x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014, gives bank accounts with insurance and a RuPay debit card, and is run by the Ministry of Finance (a, b, c); it does not grant loans to businessmen (that is MUDRA), so 'a, b & c'.

s: Which one of the following is the most effective financial inclusion programme?
x: Jan Dhan Yojana is India's flagship (world's largest) financial inclusion programme; demonetisation, Aadhaar and crop insurance are not financial inclusion programmes in that sense.

Quantitative Restrictions imposed by India on import of certain goods

s:
Consider the following statements in respect of RTGS and NEFT :
I. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments.
II. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.
III. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: RTGS settles instantly while NEFT settles in batches (I true); neither charges for inward credits (II false), and both run 24x7x365 (RTGS since 14 Dec 2020), so III is false – 'I only'.

s: Which one of the following links all the ATMs in India?
x: The National Financial Switch, run by NPCI since 2009, links all ATMs in India; IBA, NSDL and the RBI do not.

s:

II. NPCI has launched RuPay, a card payment scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NPCI helps promote financial inclusion (AePS, UPI, RuPay) and launched the RuPay card scheme, so both statements are correct.

providing loans to poor farmers for cultivating
providing pensions to old and destitute persons

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Self-Help Group (SHG) programme was originally initiated by the State Bank of India by providing microcredit to the financially deprived.
2. In an SHG, all members of a group take responsibility for a loan that an individual member takes.
3. The Regional Rural Banks and Scheduled Commercial Banks support SHGs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong – the SHG-bank linkage programme was started by NABARD (1992), not SBI; members share responsibility for each other's loans and RRBs and commercial banks support SHGs, so only two statements are correct.

s: The Reserve Bank of India published Financial Inclusion Index in August 2022. According to the report the raise in the value of Financial Inclusion Index from March 2021 to March 2022 is
x: The RBI's FI-Index for March 2022 (published August 2022) was 56.4, up from 53.9 in March 2021, so the rise was '53.9 to 56.4'; 59.3 and 54.9 are wrong figures.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RBI's Digital Payments Index (RBI-DPI):

I. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been publishing the RBI-DPI with 2021 as the base year to capture the extent of digitisation of payments across the country.

II. The RBI-DPI consists of 6 broad parameters that have in turn sub-parameters.

III. There has been a constant increase in the RBI-DPI since the time of its inception.

IV. 'Consumer Centricity is one of the parameters in the RBI-DPI.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid?
x: The RBI-DPI has March 2018 (not 2021) as base and 5 (not 6) parameters, so I and II are false; it has risen every period since launch and 'consumer centricity' is a parameter – 'III and IV'.

s: Which of the following best describes the term "Merchant Discount Rate" sometimes seen in the news?
o: The incentive given by a bank to a merchant for accepting payments through debit cards pertaining to
The amount paid back by banks to their customers when they use debit cards for financial transactions
The charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments from his customers through the bank's debit
The incentive given by the Government to merchants for promoting digital payments by their customers
x: MDR is the charge a bank levies on a merchant for accepting card payments from customers; it is not an incentive or a refund.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the three key sub-indices of the Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) of RBI?
o: Credit access, Insurance depth and Banking access
Financial literacy, Access, Usage and Quality
x: The RBI FI-Index has three sub-indices – Access (35%), Usage (45%) and Quality (20%); financial literacy is folded into Quality, not a separate sub-index.

s:
Consider the following statements. The Reserve Bank of India’s recent directives relating to ‘Storage of Payment System Data, popularly known as Data Diktat, command the payment system providers that

I. they shall ensure that the entire data relating to payment systems operated by them are stored in a system only in India.

II. they shall ensure that the systems are owned and operated by public sector enterprises.

III. they shall submit the consolidated system audit report to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India by the end of the calendar year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The RBI's April 2018 directive requires the entire payment-system data to be stored only in India (I); it does not require public-sector ownership or a CAG audit – 'Only I'.

o: UPI is a real-time payment system but Digital Rupee is akin to sovereign paper currency.

s:
With reference to ‘Bitcoins’, sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is / are correct?
1. Bitcoins are tracked by the central banks of the countries.
2. Anyone with a Bitcoin address can send and receive Bitcoins from anyone else with a Bitcoin address.
3. Online payments can be sent without either side knowing the identity of the other.

x: Bitcoins are not tracked or issued by central banks (1 wrong); anyone with a Bitcoin address can transact with anyone else, and payments can be made without either side knowing the other's identity – '2 and 3 only'.

Why is the offering of "teaser loans" by commercial banks a cause of economic concern?

A. The teaser loans are considered to be an aspect of subprime lending and banks may be exposed to the risk of defaulters in future.

B. In India, the teaser loans are mostly given to inexperienced entrepreneurs to set up manufacturing or export units.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Teaser loans (cheap fixed rate at first, higher later) are a form of sub-prime lending that exposes banks to future defaults; in India they were home loans, not loans to new entrepreneurs, so A only.

the prolonged over-valuation of local currencies vis-
